C-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-2.Summary:
Deliver a generic platform enhancement to `worldline-kernel` by adding explicit capability provider targeting by `InstallationId`.
This change addresses the platform gap discovered during the early feasibility gate of C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904: while capability discovery can observe multiple active installations of the same capability contract, invocation previously always executed the default deterministic resolver (which sorts by highest compatible minor, then lowest installation ID, then runtime ID). Consequently, secondary active installations were unreachable through capability invocations.
This change introduces an additive `CapabilityTarget` model: `CapabilityTarget::AnyCompatible` (existing deterministic default resolution) and `CapabilityTarget::Installation(InstallationId)` (explicit target routing). The target binds to the durable `InstallationId`, never to ephemeral `RuntimeId`. At invocation time, the broker resolves the target `InstallationId` to its current live `RuntimeId`, enforcing normal admission and authority checks without authority inheritance across restart or replacement.
The targeting mechanism enforces strict failure semantics: if the targeted installation is absent, incompatible, quarantined, deactivating, or stopped, the broker returns an explicit `TargetUnavailable` error without silent fallback to another provider. Targeting does not grant authority: the caller must independently hold authorization to invoke the capability contract.
C-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-2.Problem:
Worldline is designed as a userland operating environment where product capabilities come from plugins and multiple installations of a single plugin definition can exist with distinct installation-owned configuration (multi-install cardinality).
In the current kernel implementation: 1. `CapabilityRegistry::resolve` and `InvocationBroker::invoke` only accept a `CapabilityId` and unconditionally sort candidates to pick the first deterministic entry. 2. When two installations of the same plugin definition are simultaneously active, the candidate with the lexicographically higher `InstallationId` is permanently shadowed and cannot be reached by callers. 3. Callers have no way to express an intent to invoke a specific installation without stopping, deactivating, or unregistering other installations. 4. Storing product preferences (e.g. default search provider) in `worldline-kernel` would violate the invariant that the kernel contains no domain policy. 5. Conversely, introducing an intermediary routing plugin around an incomplete kernel primitive would add unnecessary architectural scaffolding and obscure the platform contract.
The microkernel must therefore provide a minimal, generic, policy-free addressing primitive: allow callers to invoke a capability targeted to a specific `InstallationId` while keeping selection policy, defaults, and configuration persistence in higher layers.

Goals.Goal: Add a generic `CapabilityTarget` enum to `worldline-kernel` distinguishing `CapabilityTarget::AnyCompatible` from `CapabilityTarget::Installation(InstallationId)`.

Provide public convenience API `kernel.capability_for_installation(caller, capability, installation_id)` and preserve existing `kernel.capability_for(caller, capability)` as default untargeted resolution.
Enable `CapabilityHandle` and plugin `ActivationContext` to obtain and invoke targeted capability handles without changing stable contract DTO wire forms.
Ensure targeting binds to durable `InstallationId` rather than ephemeral `RuntimeId`, resolving the live runtime at invocation admission time.

Enforce strict error semantics on targeted invocation failure: return explicit `TargetUnavailable` (or equivalent typed failure) when the target installation is missing, stopped, deactivating, quarantined, or incompatible, with zero silent fallback.
Preserve capability security invariants: targeting an installation conveys zero authority; callers must hold regular capability authorization for the contract and operation.
Prove two simultaneously active installations of the same plugin definition can be independently invoked through explicit targeting without consumer provider-name branching.
Record the architectural decision and evidence in docs/adr/ADR-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-V1.md.

Constraints.Constraint: TARGETING BINDS TO DURABLE INSTALLATION_ID, NEVER TO EPHEMERAL RUNTIME_ID.
NO PREFERRED-PROVIDER TABLE OR SELECTION POLICY PERSISTENCE IN WORLDLINE-KERNEL.
NO SILENT FALLBACK TO ANOTHER PROVIDER WHEN A TARGETED INSTALLATION FAILS OR IS UNAVAILABLE.
TARGETING AN INSTALLATION CONFERS NO PRIVILEGE OR AUTHORITY BEYOND THE CALLER'S EXISTING GRANTS.
RUNTIME REPLACEMENT OR RESTART NEVER INHERITS LIVE AUTHORITY FROM THE PREVIOUS RUNTIME.
EXISTING UNTARGETED INVOCATION PATH MUST REMAIN 100% BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE AND DETERMINISTIC.
EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC AND MUST NOT BE USED FOR CAPABILITY TARGETING RESOLUTION.
AUDIT TRAJECTORY RECORDS CAPABILITY, TARGET INSTALLATION, RESOLVED RUNTIME, AND OUTCOME WITHOUT PAYLOAD LEAKAGE.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Adding a persistent preference store or "default provider" table into the microkernel.
Adding search-specific, browser-specific, or UI-specific types to worldline-kernel.
Modifying stable Browser Contract v1.0 or existing experimental browser service contracts.
Changing the existing deterministic resolution order for untargeted `AnyCompatible` requests.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `Kernel::capability_for_installation` creates a `CapabilityHandle` bound to a specific target `InstallationId`.
`CapabilityHandle` retains target identity and routes invocations to the target installation.

When two installations of the same `PluginDefinition` are simultaneously active, an untargeted handle routes to the default installation, while targeted handles route independently to installation A and installation B.
Targeted invocation of an absent or uninstalled installation fails with an explicit typed error without fallback.
Targeted invocation of a stopped, deactivating, or quarantined installation fails with an explicit typed error without fallback.
Targeted invocation of an installation providing an incompatible major interface version fails with an explicit version-mismatch error without fallback.
Restarting or replacing a targeted installation creates a fresh `RuntimeId`; subsequent targeted invocations resolve to the new runtime, while stale runtime grants/authority are not inherited.
Caller authority is verified for targeted invocations under the standard capability authorization model; lack of a matching grant results in `Denied` regardless of targeting.
Trajectory security events record the requested target installation, candidate count, resolved runtime ID, and outcome without logging private request/result payloads.
All existing unit, integration, property, security, and proving-slice tests pass without regression.
`docs/adr/ADR-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-PROVIDER-TARGETING-V1.md` documents the architecture, targeting model, failure semantics, security boundaries, and rejected alternatives.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh local test evidence proves two simultaneously active installations of the same capability can be targeted independently, restart/replacement resolves to fresh runtime without stale authority, missing/quarantined/incompatible targets fail closed without silent fallback, and all existing kernel invariants and CI gates remain green.

Assumptions.Assumption: `InstallationId` is durable across kernel restarts and uniquely identifies an installation within the local kernel instance.
Higher layers (Shell, Workspace, Browser Services) will persist user provider preferences by storing `InstallationId` rather than requiring kernel-level preference storage.
The existing untargeted resolution order remains the standard fallback for consumers that do not require explicit provider selection.
